critique: The navy/cyan/violet system is disciplined and the skill nodes, connector lines, panels, and typography largely belong to one sci-fi RPG language. Craft inconsistencies remain at the system edges: active cyan nodes use multiple glow intensities and ring constructions, while inactive nodes and the violet keystone introduce different border weights and halos. Connector strokes meet node rims somewhat awkwardly and vary in brightness, making the graph feel less precisely constructed than the surrounding panels. The tiny blue utility copy is low contrast, tab states are overly faint, and the portrait is an abstract set of circles that does not share the crisp line-icon grammar. The large empty lower portions of both sidebars make their panel rhythm feel unfinished.
suggestion: Define explicit node tokens for locked, available, selected, and keystone states using consistent diameters, two ring widths, and controlled glow levels; terminate every connector exactly beneath the outer ring and normalize line weight and color by state. Raise contrast and minimum size for labels, descriptions, inactive tabs, and stats while keeping a consistent uppercase tracking scale. Rework the portrait into the same crisp vector/stroke language, align sidebar section baselines to the central panel, and add restrained dividers or structured lower modules so the side columns feel deliberately completed rather than merely empty.
audit_note: Direct independent visual critique from the r0 screenshot and brief only; no generation notes, HTML, other critics, revisions, or scores were inspected.
